extracted.intended_audience: grassroots climate activists, movement builders, and organizers seeking grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants on what kinds of climate activism projects the Climate Emergency Fund will fund, including program-area priorities and the types of activities and organizational stages they prioritize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for disruptive, nonviolent climate activism
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate Emergency Fund supports disruptive, nonviolent climate activism because it is the fastest way to create transformative change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for actions and campaigns that are both disruptive and explicitly nonviolent; this framing is presented as the fund's primary mission and evaluative lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultra-ambitious projects
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek ultra-ambitious projects ... that build enough power to transform society and win big for a livable future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund favors proposals with high ambition and transformative potential rather than incrementalism; look for projects that aim to shift systems at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kickstarting early-stage efforts / seed funding for new movements
rubrics_metrics.description: A relatively small infusion of funds to protest groups dramatically improve their chances of liftoff. We specialize in identifying and supporting promising new movements in their earliest stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund provides seed-level support to nascent groups and campaigns; proposals from very early-stage organizers with a clear plan for growth are within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding key movement infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund key infrastructure that build enough power to transform society ... Protest movements can benefit from behind-the-scenes, professional support, including strategic consulting, training, press support, fiscal sponsorships, software, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund will support non-frontline infrastructure (training, consulting, press, fiscal sponsorship, software, etc.) that strengthens movements and increases capacity to scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fighting fossil fuels (primary program area)
rubrics_metrics.description: The vast majority of Climate Emergency Fund grants aim to end the fossil fuel economy to secure a livable future. Our grantees are grassroots groups employing a wide range of tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects explicitly targeting fossil fuel extraction, infrastructure, finance, or the fossil fuel economy broadly are the primary focus; grassroots tactics across a spectrum are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate justice and democracy strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Diverse climate movement leaders have begun piloting visionary new strategies – from debt cancelation to citizens’ assemblies, paving the way for shifting society at scale on the climate fight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund is interested in justice-centered and democratic reform approaches that link climate goals to broader social change (examples given: debt cancellation, citizens' assemblies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate Resistance Incubator participation / catalytic programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate Emergency Fund has partnered with top movement experts to create a transformative piece of movement infrastructure, which aims to catalyze the next generation of climate mass protest movements in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund supports programmatic, catalytic initiatives (like incubators) designed to accelerate and professionalize mass protest organizing; proposals that sync with or feed into such incubators may be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for demonstrable results / building people power
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grantees get results. Climate Emergency Fund grantees have proven the effectiveness of people power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should emphasize evidence of impact, capacity to grow the movement, and strategies that build people power; the Fund highlights past grantee breakthroughs as part of its expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with stated mission and questions the Fund asks
rubrics_metrics.description: Growing the climate movement? Pioneering new strategies? Building people power? Apply for a grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit selection questions: Does the proposal grow the movement, pioneer new strategies, or build people power? Applicants should frame proposals to answer these core evaluative prompts.
